Impact: allow archs more flexibility on dynamic ftrace implementations
Dynamic ftrace has largly been developed on x86. Since x86 does not
have the same limitations as other architectures
between the generic code and the architecture specific code was not
flexible enough to handle some of the issues that other architectures
have.
Most notably
column2: module trampolines. Due to the limited branch distance

column1: that archs make in calling kernel core code from modules
load code must create a trampoline to jump to what will make the
larger jump into core kernel code.
The problem arises when this happens to a call to mcount. Ftrace checks
all code before modifying it and makes sure the current code is what
it expects. Right now
column2: there is not enough information to handle modifying

column1: module trampolines.
This patch changes the API between generic dynamic ftrace code and
the arch dependent code. There is now two functions for modifying code:
ftrace_make_nop(mod
column3: addr) - convert the code at rec->ip into

column1: a nop
column2: where the original text is calling addr. (mod is the

column1: module struct if called by module init)
ftrace_make_caller(rec
column2: addr) - convert the code rec->ip that should

column1: be a nop into a caller to addr.
The record ""rec"" now has a new field called ""arch"" where the architecture
can add any special attributes to each call site record.
